clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute longitudinal extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) secondary to COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with acute onset back pain, bilateral leg numbness/paresthesia, inability to walk, urinary retention, and constipation, 5 days after testing positive for SARS-CoV-2. Neurological examination revealed exaggerated reflexes, positive Babinski's sign, lower extremity weakness, and sensory impairment. MRI of the spine showed T2-weighted lesions and multiple regions of patchy hyperintensity in the thoracic spinal cord, later confirmed as 'long-segment myelopathy'. CSF analysis was negative for infectious agents (including SARS-CoV-2 PCR), aquaporin-4 antibodies, anti-MOG antibodies, and oligoclonal bands, with normal cell count and protein. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone, followed by oral prednisolone, and showed clinical improvement, mobilizing short distances independently by discharge. The diagnosis of acute longitudinal extensive transverse myelitis was made, with the temporal association to recent COVID-19 infection and exclusion of other causes supporting a post-infectious, immune-mediated etiology.
